definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese sweet made from white bean paste mixed with a small amount of {求肥|ぎゅうひ} (mochi-based binder), then kneaded, tinted, and shaped by hand — often into flowers or seasonal motifs.

examples.japanese: {練|ね}り{切|き}り⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べた→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
{練|ね}り{切|き}り⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{茶道|さどう}→茶道：04451_sadou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{出|だ}される→出す：01087_dasu⟧。
examples.english: Nerikiri is often served at tea ceremony.

examples.japanese: ⟦{季節|きせつ}→季節：01304_kisetsu⟧ごと⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{桜|さくら}→桜：02212_sakura⟧や⟦{紅葉|もみじ}→紅葉：05387_momiji⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{形|かたち}→形：02193_katachi⟧にした{練|ね}り{切|き}り⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{店頭|てんとう}→店頭：12488_tentou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{並|なら}ぶ→並ぶ：00605_narabu⟧。
examples.english: Each season, nerikiri shaped like cherry blossoms or maple leaves line the shop displays.

notes:
A category of {上生菓子|じょうなまがし} (high-grade fresh wagashi) and a staple of formal tea ceremony. Shapes are seasonal — plum and pine for New Year, cherry blossoms for spring, chrysanthemums for autumn.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {上生菓子|じょうなまがし}: high-grade fresh wagashi — broader category that includes {練|ね}り{切|き}り
- ⟦{和菓子|わがし}→和菓子：04962_wagashi⟧: Japanese sweets (general) — the umbrella term
- ⟦{饅頭|まんじゅう}→饅頭：05000_manjuu⟧: manju — steamed bun with filling; a different style of wagashi
